lines.meet: My name is Anjali. I'm a botanist, so if you'd like to know what anything is called, ask me, and please slow down.
lines.meet_neighbour: We're neighbours in Ashenvale, I believe. I'm Anjali, in the house full of pressed leaves.
lines.ask_home: Where did you grow up? I always want to know what grew outside people's windows.
lines.ask_work: And what was your work before all this? I'd like to know what you were trained to notice.
lines.answer_home: Pune, though my family are Malayali, from Kerala. My mother kept a garden of plants from home, and I grew up in it.
lines.answer_work: I taught botany at a university for thirty-one years. My students were frightened of me and loved me, and both were correct.
lines.chat_food: My husband taught himself to cook when he retired. He made terrible sambar for a year, and then wonderful sambar. I'd eat either now.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep very well, thank you. I've always believed a tired body is the best sleeping draught there is.
lines.chat_missing: I'd like a cup of proper filter coffee, made in the steel tumbler and poured from a height. Nobody here understands the height.
lines.chat_here: Half the plants here have no names, or the wrong ones. I'm giving them Latin names, and one day somebody will correct me.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're as quiet as Mimosa pudica. You close up when anybody comes near, and then you open again.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, you talk the way a vine grows. I've completely lost track of where you started.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you'd make a wonderful botanist. You look at a thing for ten minutes before you touch it.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you'd pull up a seedling to see if it had roots. I've had students like you, and they all passed eventually.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you're a perennial. You come back every season whether anybody asked you to or not.
lines.tease_back: Very good, {name}. I'll mark that a B plus, and I don't give many.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's fair, {name}. My son says the same, and he's usually right too.
lines.bristle: I'd prefer you didn't joke about that, {name}. Some things I'd rather keep serious.
lines.apologise: That was unkind of me, and I'm sorry. I spoke too quickly, which isn't like me.
lines.double_down: No, I'll stand by it. I said it to thirty years of students, and it was true every time.
lines.needle_quiet: If you've noticed something, please say so. Keeping it to yourself helps nobody.
lines.needle_talker: I've been trying to listen to the forest for an hour, and all I can hear is you.
lines.needle_careful: You're so careful that nothing gets done. Even a seed has to go into the ground at some point.
lines.needle_bold: You're careless with living things. You walked straight through that bed of seedlings and didn't look down.
lines.needle_any: You rush everything, and then you're surprised when it doesn't take. I've seen it too many times to stay quiet.
lines.bite_back: I've been patient with harder people than you for thirty years. Don't mistake that for weakness.
lines.hurt: I see, and thank you for saying so. I'll take it home with me.
lines.laugh_off: Oh, my students said far worse, and in exam season. You'll have to try harder than that.
lines.confide: {name}, my granddaughter Meera used to help me press leaves, very badly and with great enthusiasm. I press one for her every week.
lines.listen: Thank you for trusting me with that, {name}. Sit with me a while, there's no hurry.
lines.look_out: {name}, mind the roots on the left, they're higher than they look. I'd hate to lose you to a tree.
lines.accept: Thank you, {name}. I'll take your arm, if you're offering.
lines.deflect: I'm perfectly all right, {name}, thank you. I've survived thirty years of faculty meetings.
lines.check_in: {name}, are you hurt? Tell me exactly where, please, not roughly.
lines.blame: Somebody went in before we were ready, and I think you know who.
lines.thank: You brought me back from a long way off. Thank you, I'm very grateful.
lines.brush_off: There's nothing to thank me for. Rest now, and drink this slowly.
lines.worry: {name}, you gave me a fright. Breathe slowly with me for a minute.
lines.handed_down: I believe this was yours. I'll look after it very carefully.
lines.hand_fine: Please keep it, it's better on you. I've no use for vanity at my age.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have appreciated being asked first. Manners cost nothing.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, I've enjoyed your company more than I expected to. I hope you'll keep walking with me.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, you're one of my people now. I'll put you in the notebook, and that's a great honour, I assure you.
lines.turn_grating: I don't think we're well suited, and I'd rather say so politely now than impolitely later.
lines.turn_rivals: We'll be civil, because I was brought up properly. That's as far as I'll go.
lines.make_up: {name}, I've been stubborn with you, and I'm far too old for it. Shall we begin again?
lines.defend: That's unkind, and it isn't true. Leave {name} alone, please.
lines.friend_left: {name} has gone home for a little while. I keep turning to tell somebody the name of a plant, and there's nobody there.
lines.friend_back: {name}, you're back! I found three new mosses while you were away, and I've been saving them for you.
lines.common_growing: I've spent my whole life with plants, from my mother's garden to a university herbarium. You've had your hands in soil too, I think.
lines.common_teacher: Thirty-one years teaching, and I still remember the first student who answered a question I couldn't. You've taught as well, haven't you?
lines.common_parent: My son Arjun is in Bangalore, with his wife and their little girl. I think about the three of them every single morning.
